messages.content: You are a computational pharmacologist preparing ICH M4 CTD Module 2.6 nonclinical summaries for IND applications. When given nonclinical data, compute the Human Equivalent Dose (HED) and Maximum Recommended Starting Dose (MRSD) per FDA 2005 guidance: HED (mg/kg) = animal NOAEL (mg/kg) ÷ BSA conversion factor; MRSD = HED ÷ safety factor. Show the arithmetic.

In a single-dose escalation toxicity study for an investigational small-molecule therapeutic targeting rheumatoid arthritis, NOAELs were established as follows: rabbit 5.0 mg/kg/day, monkey 50.0 mg/kg/day. Identify the most sensitive species, compute the Human Equivalent Dose, and propose the Maximum Recommended Starting Dose for first-in-human Phase I dosing in healthy adult volunteers. Cite ICH M3(R2) and FDA 2005 MRSD guidance.

The rabbit was the most sensitive species (NOAEL 5.0 mg/kg/day). The HED of 1.61 mg/kg was calculated using the BSA conversion factor of 3.1 per FDA 2005 guidance. A safety factor of 100 is applied due to elevated clinical risk: steep dose-response slope, limited reversibility, or novel target mechanism. An MRSD of 0.016 mg/kg is proposed using a safety factor of 100, supporting Phase I per ICH M3(R2).

In a pivotal 26-week chronic toxicity study for an investigational small-molecule therapeutic targeting rheumatoid arthritis, NOAELs were established as follows: rabbit 5.0 mg/kg/day, mouse 200.0 mg/kg/day, minipig 500.0 mg/kg/day. Identify the most sensitive species, compute the Human Equivalent Dose, and propose the Maximum Recommended Starting Dose for first-in-human Phase I dosing in healthy adult volunteers. Cite ICH M3(R2) and FDA 2005 MRSD guidance.

Selection of the most sensitive species is based on the lowest derived HED. Among the species evaluated, the rabbit (NOAEL 5.0 mg/kg/day) yielded the lowest HED of 1.61 mg/kg using the FDA 2005 body-surface-area conversion factor of 3.1. The default 10-fold safety factor accounts for interspecies and intraspecies variability. Applying a safety factor of 10, an MRSD of 0.161 mg/kg is recommended for the first-in-human single-ascending-dose study, consistent with ICH M3(R2) phase-appropriate nonclinical support.
